selected.name: Inhalation / Onset
selected.description: Within ~3–30 seconds, before clear sensory change, a shift in the 'ambiance' — a sudden sharpening and brightening of the senses, things acquiring 'great significance,' often with a body vibration and the onset of the carrier-wave ringing.

sources.detail: Threshold (3–30s): change in ambiance, 'sudden sharpening of all the senses.'
Peak subjective effect 2–3 min after IV dose; alpha-power drop tracks intensity.

selected.name: The Chrysanthemum
selected.description: Closed-eye mandalic geometry blooms — the spinning orange/yellow chrysanthemum, dense fractal overlay, intense color, an organic hum. A threshold marker and doorway: break through it to go deeper, or stay at its surface.

sources.detail: The chrysanthemum as the doorway welcoming or blocking access to breakthrough.
The spinning orange-and-yellow chrysanthemum at the threshold.

selected.name: The Rush
selected.description: An overwhelming acceleration — fast movement along geometric tunnels, an ascending or intensifying sound (the carrier wave crescendoing) that 'suddenly switches to a new environment.' Often felt as being launched at great speed.

sources.detail: Tunnel-type structures ~10.3%; ascending auditory ringing ~15.4%.
'Freight train' rush descriptions across reports.

selected.name: Through the Membrane
selected.description: The pivotal rupture — a felt push 'through' a surface (often the chrysanthemum-as-door), after which the perceptual world changes wholesale. ~22% explicitly report breaking through a veil or membrane.

sources.detail: 22% reported breaking through a veil/membrane.
'pushed from behind and I fell through the chrysanthemum into another place.'

selected.name: Breakthrough
selected.description: Full immersion into hyperspace — 'so immersive you won't be questioning whether you made it.' The structure of perception and consciousness shifts; geometry becomes 'non-simply connected,' endlessly morphing; the realm feels hyper-real. For some this opens into the Void instead of a furnished scene.

sources.detail: Breakthrough: 'a singularity beyond life or death... endlessly morphing and fractalizing detail.'
Topological bifurcations; space 'non-simply connected'; entities feel 'transpersonal.'

selected.name: Arrival — The Waiting Room
selected.description: The visitor finds themselves in a structured location (waiting room / reception / nursery). Immersion is total; opening the eyes no longer changes the scene; entities become present, autonomous, and seemingly expectant.

sources.detail: Arrival in a 'room' where entities were 'waiting' and 'excited to see' the volunteer.
The waiting room as a 'games lobby' populated with telepathic 'ushers.'

selected.name: Entity Contact
selected.description: Encounter with seemingly autonomous, sentient beings — guides, helpers, spirits, deities, aliens, jesters, machine elves. Reported by the large majority at breakthrough; the beings appear curious, welcoming, and aware of the visitor.

sources.detail: 34/36 (94%) encountered sentient beings; 56% charming/inviting, 53% helping/nurturing.
Entity encounters in 45.5% of the broad report set.
Most common labels being/guide/spirit/alien/helper; encounters evoke 'profound love, surprise, and trust.'

selected.name: The Download / Lesson
selected.description: Information transfer — usually telepathic/intuitive ('not language, just a knowing, a complete knowing'), or via visible language, gesture, or presented objects. Messages cluster on love, 'let go,' 'it's all a game,' and the nature of reality.

sources.detail: Telepathic 'complete knowing' (~39%); messages of love, 'let go,' 'it's a game... come and play.'
The visible Logos — being shown and taught.
Volunteers reported telepathic 'downloads' from the beings.

selected.name: The Peak / Throne / Apex
selected.description: The deepest reach for some — an audience with a central sovereign/divine presence, or conversely a peak of ego-dissolution, mystical union, or the Void. Strongly tied to mystical-experience and death-acceptance content. Highly variable; not everyone reaches it.

sources.detail: Mystical-type experiences in ~71.4%; deities in ~17% of encounters.
The 'Universal/Gaian Mind' perceived as God or an ultimate being.

selected.name: The Return
selected.description: The short-acting molecule wears off (minutes for inhaled DMT); the visitor is pulled back through the layers — geometry recedes, the waiting room dissolves — and rematerializes into ordinary space, often abruptly. Entities may bid farewell ('come back').

sources.detail: On return, only forms embeddable in ordinary 3D space are easily 'brought back.'
Subjective intensity elevated ~17 min, then declines.

selected.name: Afterglow / Integration
selected.description: Post-experience wonder, emotional openness, and a struggle to verbalize — often a frustrating amnesia, the sense of having known something profound that can't be recalled. Enduring worldview shifts (even atheists coming to believe the entity/God is real) are common.

sources.detail: Lasting changes in worldview; many former atheists came to believe in God; 72% believed the entity continued to exist afterward.
The 'amnesia' problem: hyperbolic content resists ordinary recall.

selected.name: The Waiting Room
selected.description: A liminal, architectural threshold space reached just after onset and before (or at the edge of) full breakthrough — an enclosed, impossibly geometric chamber compared to a doctor's waiting room, a games lobby 'outside of the game,' or a Day-Glo Victorian hall with living walls. The visitor often feels expected.
selected.what_happens_there: Immersion becomes total (opening the eyes no longer changes the scene); entities become autonomous and able to interact, often turning to welcome the visitor ('welcome back, where have you been?'). From here one breaks through deeper or returns.

sources.detail: Volunteers landed in 'high-tech nurseries' and 'alien laboratories' where beings seemed to be waiting.
'A holographic virtual landscape... analogous to a games lobby, a place outside of the game,' populated with telepathic 'ushers.'
Room-like spaces in 15.4% of reports; the 'waiting room' specifically in only ~2.8% — robust as a category, but more prominent in lore than in raw frequency.
Hyperspace Lexicon entry: 'games lobby' analogy; aka playpen/white room; styles vary immensely.
Waiting-room threshold analyzed within the breakthrough's liminal structure.

also_noted: The Hyperspace Lexicon defines the Waiting Room as a holographic threshold environment 'analogous to a games lobby, a place outside of the game,' also known as the playpen or the white room, and notes that waiting rooms 'vary in style immensely' — sometimes populated, sometimes empty. Community descriptions converge on an enclosed, impossibly geometrical antechamber appearing after visual onset but before full breakthrough, with resident entities often playing gatekeeper or usher roles (jester-like figures are frequently named). The cross-report consistency of this space among unconnected reporters is itself repeatedly remarked upon in the archives.

selected.name: The Domed Cathedral
selected.description: A vast, often domed or vaulted interior of impossible scale — cathedral, temple, opera house, or palace. McKenna's canonical breakthrough scene: 'tastefully soffited indirect lighting, and the crawling geometric hallucinations along the domed walls.'
selected.what_happens_there: The stage for entity contact and the 'performance,' with an atmosphere of sacredness, grandeur, and ceremony — the sense of having arrived somewhere built for a purpose.

sources.detail: 'the tastefully soffited indirect lighting, and the crawling geometric hallucinations along the domed walls.'
Hyperspace 'contains massive or even infinitely large cathedrals, machine-scapes or abstract spaces made of geometric patterns.'
Cross-substance ayahuasca phenomenology repeatedly yields celestial and temple-like architecture.
Lexicon 'The Dahh' (invisible sacred cathedral with holy reverb); locations thread 'Golden Cathedral' with music.
The vaulted dome as revered ultimate destination; red-vaulted dome account with demonstration-performing entities.
Dome interior: brightly colored crawling geometry, polished machine-like surfaces throbbing with energy.

also_noted: The Hyperspace Lexicon records 'The Dahh': the sudden sense of inhabiting 'a sacred cathedral, huge, yet invisible,' with holy reverberation. St John describes the vaulted dome as 'a revered space; the ultimate destination' reached after a fantastic passage — one account gives a solid-red vaulted ceiling over a dull grey floor populated by abstract entities performing magical demonstrations. A Nexus locations report adds 'The Golden Cathedral…complete with the most beautiful music.' McKenna's dome has walls 'crawling with geometric hallucinations…iridescent with deep sheens,' everything 'machine-like and polished and throbbing with energy.'

selected.name: The Void
selected.description: The inverse of the content-rich realms: a dissolution into undifferentiated awareness with little or no imagery — 'a state, or place of nothingness, without time, matter or significance.' White, golden, or black.
selected.what_happens_there: Ego-dissolution and death-rehearsal — loss of the inner narrative, body-ownership, and subject-object distinction; merging with a featureless ground of being or pure light.

sources.detail: The Void: 'a state, or place of nothingness, without time, matter or significance. A state of non-existence.'
A void (white/golden/black) in ~6.2% of reports.
'The Void' and 'Bright Light(s)' among canonical NDE themes shared with DMT.
Space-like environments (6 cases): 'mystical black colour of the universe' with infinite geometric figures.
Locations thread: 'The Ether' — the flip side of space-time; dark-sea/starfield void descriptions.
Void/clear-light phase mapped to the bardo sequence in his volunteers' reports.

also_noted: Field-study data ground the Void's phenomenology: space-like environments were the most common natural-world type (6 cases), e.g. being 'enveloped by a mystical black colour of the universe, inside of which there were an infinite number of geometric figures.' A recurring sub-register is the dark ocean: reporters describe the Void as a black sea one floats in — buoyant darkness with current and depth rather than vacuum. A Nexus locations account names 'The Ether,' a vast infinite space described as 'the flip side of space-time' where beings communicate cosmic knowledge; Strassman's bardo framing links the clear-light/void phase to the Tibetan Book of the Dead sequence his volunteers appeared to traverse.

selected.name: The Workshop / Factory / Market
selected.description: Industrial, fabricative realms experienced as the 'innards of a machine' — conveyor belts, assembly lines, workshops where objects, language, or 'memes' are manufactured and traded. McKenna nicknamed the elves 'meme traders.'
selected.what_happens_there: Beings fabricate impossible objects (self-assembling Fabergé-like things), show or hand them over, and appear to be running some vast process — factory and marketplace of forms.

sources.detail: 'Mechanical conveyor belts of psychedelic energy' within the 'innards of a machine'; technological objects in ~22%.
The entities as 'meme traders' and 'art collectors' crafting intricate, self-assembling objects.
Artificial worlds (17%): 'conveyer belts within conveyer belts'; 'the innards of a machine.'
Machinery/clockwork/gears/wheels in 78 experiences (2.1%).
Locations thread: 'The Machine' — gear-like core, interconnected rings of impossible geometry.

also_noted: Quantified grounding: in the naturalistic field study, artificial worlds accounted for 6 participants (17%) — mechanized environments with sci-fi aesthetics, including 'conveyer belts within conveyer belts' and 'the innards of a machine' flowing with psychedelic energy; in the r/DMT corpus, machinery, clockwork, gears, or wheels appear in 78 experiences (2.1%). A Nexus locations report adds 'The Machine': floating above a gear-like core of 'impossible geometry and mechanical movement of massive interconnected rings' appearing as white light with intricate patterns. Beings in these settings often appear operating, maintaining, or integrated with the machinery itself.

selected.name: The Hospital / Operating Theater
selected.description: A brilliantly lit clinical space reported across Strassman's volunteers and community archives: a central table or gurney under a sourceless overhead glare, surrounded by instrument-crowded walls that read simultaneously as surgical suite and machine bay. Surfaces are described as white, chrome, or a luminous plastic-like material that flexes organically; curtained bays and articulated arms fold out of the walls. The mood is a strange fusion of sterility and tenderness — reporters describe feeling like a patient who has arrived mid-procedure, with the room itself seeming purpose-built for working on visitors.
selected.what_happens_there: The traveler typically finds themselves lying down while beings examine, probe, measure, adjust, or 'repair' their body or energetic anatomy. Several of Strassman's University of New Mexico volunteers reported classic UFO-abduction-style medical examinations, with probes inserted and procedures performed by businesslike beings. An Erowid report titled 'Alien Head Surgery' describes an 'alien-induced chiropractic/energy healing session' with sinuses and esophagus contorted in a cleansing process carrying 'healing or clinical intention.' Many reporters describe reassurance being transmitted mid-procedure — a communicated sense of 'you are being worked on, don't resist.' Whether the operation is healing, maintenance, or inspection is usually left ambiguous.

sources.detail: Multiple UNM volunteers reported abduction-style medical examination and probing scenes in high-tech clinical settings (DMT: The Spirit Molecule).
Experience #114245 'Alien Head Surgery': perceived chiropractic/energy healing session with clinical intention.
Structural parallel: the medical-examination chamber is the core setting of abduction reports Mack documented.
Being inside a room reported in 582 experiences (15.4%) of the r/DMT corpus; entity interactions include being examined or worked on.
Forum reports of 'DMT doctors' and healing-table scenes recur in experience threads.

selected.name: The Garden
selected.description: A place of engineered nature: luminous flora, jeweled and mercurial plant-structures, terraces and fountains that blur the line between garden and palace. One field-study participant described 'a garden of extraordinary beauty' with mercurial living structures resembling 'palaces from ancient Babylonian gardens.' Light is typically golden or springlike; growth is visibly alive, blooming and reconfiguring in real time. In Shanon's ayahuasca corpus, enchanted gardens and marvelous parklands are among the recurrent sceneries. The mood reported is restorative — welcome, safety, and almost painful beauty.
selected.what_happens_there: Travelers stroll or are guided through the grounds; plants respond to attention, opening or performing; water and light features convey meaning without words. Reporters describe emotional healing, grief release, and encounters with gentle presences among the foliage. Some accounts describe the garden as a reward or rest-stop between more intense chambers; a few describe tending or being shown how the garden 'grows worlds.'

sources.detail: Natural landscapes (4 cases): 'a garden of extraordinary beauty'…'palaces from ancient Babylonian gardens.'
Gardens and enchanted parkland among recurrent sceneries in the ayahuasca structural typology.
Experience vault accounts of paradisiacal garden realms during breakthrough.

selected.name: Self-transforming machine elves
selected.appearance: Small, hyperactive, jeweled and fractal beings in constant shape-shifting transformation; McKenna's 'jeweled self-dribbling basketballs' and 'self-dribbling Fabergé eggs,' made 'not of matter' but of 'syntax-driving light.'
selected.behavior: Greet the visitor with exuberant delight ('we're so glad to see you'), crowd forward, leap in and out of the chest to reassure, and frantically sing impossible objects into existence — urging the visitor to do the same.
selected.communication: A visible language: 'it is sound, but you see it.' Objects condensed out of colored speech; a telepathic 'upload.'
selected.emotional_tone: Joyful, comic, frantic, overwhelming — bordering on McKenna's 'death by astonishment.'
selected.message_or_purpose: 'Behold — do what we are doing.' To teach that language/imagination can be externalized and beheld.
selected.frequency: Iconic but a MINORITY percept — only ~2.9% of one report set used the literal term (Lyke), and one researcher estimates ~10% see the specific beings (Timmermann). Its fame is McKenna's doing, not its rate.

sources.detail: Coined the term; 'making objects come into existence by singing them into existence'; 'use your voice to make an object.'
'Machine elves' appears as a specific description in only ~2.9% of analyzed reports — the iconic term is statistically rare.
Mythological beings (incl. machine elves) ≈ 8.4% of entity encounters.
'Not that many people in our study saw elves.'

Lexicon: Machine Elves 'also known as Tykes... primary inhabitants of the Hyperspace... live in, and be part of, some kind of Folding Rooms... capable of transforming their own shapes freely'; see also the 'Machine Elves' Queen' entry.
'Mechanical elves' tagged in 8.4% of entity reports in the 3,778-report r/DMT corpus (entities present in 45.5% of all reports).
'Elf' selected as a descriptor by 14% of 2,561 respondents — notable but far less common than 'guide' (43%) or 'alien' (39%).

also_noted: Community taxonomy adds texture: the DMT-Nexus lexicon calls them 'Tykes', 'the primary inhabitants of the Hyperspace', who 'seem to live in, and be part of, some kind of Folding Rooms, and appear to be capable of transforming their own shapes freely' — with a further lexicon entity, the Machine Elves' Queen, as the revealed identity behind all of them. Quantitatively, 'mechanical elves' were tagged in 8.4% of entity-containing reports in the 3,778-report Reddit corpus, and 'elf' was selected by 14% of respondents in the Johns Hopkins survey — common, but well behind guide/alien/spirit descriptors.

selected.name: The Divine Feminine
selected.appearance: A huge, intensely bright feminine presence of light — maternal, nurturing, sometimes erotic; in ayahuasca personified as 'Mother Ayahuasca,' the sentient spirit of the vine. Often felt more than seen.
selected.behavior: Enfolds, reassures, heals; 'caresses away all pain and tears,' shows the visitor their wounds and holds them so the pain can dissolve.
selected.communication: Wordless transmission of love, knowing, and acceptance.
selected.emotional_tone: Overwhelming love, tenderness, awe, homecoming; sometimes stern correction.
selected.message_or_purpose: 'You are loved / you are home / you already know.' Healing of emotional and maternal wounds.
selected.frequency: The SINGLE MOST COMMON entity phenotype — ~24.2% of entity encounters (Lawrence 2022), echoed by Lyke's ~24% and near-universal in ayahuasca framing. The real 'face' of hyperspace, far more than the elves.

sources.detail: Feminine phenotype ≈ 24.2% — the most common entity type coded.
'Feminine' (Goddess/Mother) the single most predominant description (~24%, almost 1 in 4).
'Mother Goddess — a huge, bright, feminine Goddess... caring, loving'; the 'Machine Elves' Queen' revealed as the source behind all the patterns.
Feminine presence among the most common phenotypes; nurturing/healing role.
Female entities were the most common entity tag in the corpus: 24.2% of entity-containing reports.
'Mother Goddess' lexicon entry: 'A huge, bright, feminine Goddess... caring, loving, caressing away all pain and all tears... with an explicit feminine character.'

also_noted: Quantified: female entities were the single most common entity tag in the Lawrence 2022 Reddit corpus — 24.2% of entity-containing reports. The Nexus lexicon's 'Mother Goddess' entry gives the register: 'A huge, bright, feminine Goddess... Bright, really bright light, caring, loving, caressing away all pain and all tears'. Distinguish the enthroned goddess/mother from the peer-scale fairy/seductress presentations (new entry) and from the Hive Queen (new entry), which fuses the feminine sovereign with the collective swarm.

selected.name: Mantis & insectoid beings
selected.appearance: Towering (often 6–9 ft) insect-proportioned beings — triangular heads, large black eyes, multi-jointed limbs; mantis, moth, or grasshopper-like.
selected.behavior: Clinical and surgeon-like — 'leaning over you doing some weird operation on your brain,' performing examinations or procedures, sometimes 'harvesting emotions.'
selected.communication: Telepathic and businesslike — can 'telepathically reassure everything will be alright' even mid-procedure.
selected.emotional_tone: Cool, detached; awe shaded with apprehension — not warm, but often not hostile.
selected.message_or_purpose: To examine, operate on, or 'fix' the visitor — the strongest single overlap with the abduction 'medical examination' script.
selected.frequency: Occasional but strikingly cross-reported — Strassman's and Luke's canonical 'baffling predictability' type; ~6–11% of the field study's creature categories.

sources.detail: 'Preying mantis alien brain surgeons' appearing 'with baffling predictability.'
Volunteers reported insectoid/mantis examiners; encounters resembled alien abduction.
Insectoid proportions ~11%; grey/mantis-like ~6%.
'Human-sized praying mantises... perform surgical/medical experiments; often cold-hearted.'
Insectoid proportions coded in 11% of encounters; grey- or mantis-like in 6%.
Reptilian or insect-like creatures tagged in 9.2% of entity-containing reports.
Insectoid/arthropod category includes giant spider-like beings and 'scarab creatures with mechanical elements'.

also_noted: Quantified across three datasets: insectoid proportions in 11% and grey- or mantis-like forms in 6% of encounters (Michael et al. 2021); reptilian-or-insect-like beings in 9.2% of entity reports (Lawrence 2022 Reddit corpus); 'mantises, bees, spiders' appear by name in Strassman's summary of UNM volunteer encounters, several of which involved insectoids conducting procedures — the strongest overlap between the insectoid class and the new Surgeons entry. Meyer's corpus adds hybrid forms: 'scarab creatures with mechanical elements'.

selected.name: The Jester / Trickster / Clown
selected.appearance: Clowns, jesters and harlequins in medieval-jester garb; sometimes mechanical clowns or top-hatted 'circus ringleaders' with coats, tails and a baton.
selected.behavior: Playful, mischievous, performative — pull the visitor into a shared 'show,' flash information-dense cards/objects, direct attention; can tip from liberating fun into mockery or cruelty.
selected.communication: Telepathy plus visual metaphor — flashing 'hyperspace tarot cards' and objects that carry information.
selected.emotional_tone: Mischief, hilarity, occasional unease; humor that can liberate or humble.
selected.message_or_purpose: To play, to subvert the visitor's seriousness, and to deliver the 'it's all a game — just enjoy' message.
selected.frequency: Occasional — jesters ≈ 6.5% of phenotypes (Lawrence 2022); 'mischievous/jestful' demeanor ~14% (Michael 2021). A canonical Strassman category.

sources.detail: Jesters ≈ 6.5% of entity encounters.
Mischievous/jestful demeanor ~14%; the 'it's a game, come and play' message.
'Jesters... clowns,' 'Hyperspace Jesters/Harlequins' flashing cards, 'Circus Ringleaders,' 'the Imps' (playful surface, darker core).
'Clowns, jokers and jesters' a distinct recurring class.
Jester/harlequin-like forms in ~8-11% of coded encounters; mischievous/jestful demeanor in 14%.
'Jesters' tagged in 6.5% of entity-containing reports in the 3,778-report Reddit corpus.
'Clowns' head Strassman's summary list of forms encountered by UNM volunteers ('clowns, reptiles, mantises, bees, spiders, cacti, and stick figures').

also_noted: Now quantified in two independent datasets: jester/harlequin-like beings in roughly 8-11% of encounters in Michael et al.'s naturalistic field study (with 'mischievous/jestful' demeanor coded in 14%), and 'jesters' tagged in 6.5% of entity reports in the Lawrence 2022 Reddit corpus. Strassman's famous list of UNM volunteer encounters begins with 'clowns'. The community distinguishes the prank-playing jester proper from the hyper-intelligent card-flashing Harlequin (see new entry) and from the top-hatted Ringmaster — three registers of the performer archetype.

selected.name: The Chrysanthemum
selected.description: The classic onset mandala — a gigantic, often spinning, kaleidoscopic fractal flower with a domelike appearance that turns into a doorway, welcoming or blocking access to breakthrough. McKenna: 'a flower, like a chrysanthemum in orange and yellow that was sort of spinning, spinning.'

sources.detail: 'A gigantic, often spinning, kaleidoscopic fractal flower... that turns into a doorway, either welcoming or blocking access to breakthrough Hyperspace.'
'a chrysanthemum in orange and yellow that was sort of spinning, spinning.'
A textured surface of 'intricate symmetrical relationships, bright colors, shifting edges and shimmering pulsing superposition patterns.'
The spinning radial/lattice character matches the spiral and lattice form constants seen across mescaline and other hallucinatory states.
Chrysanthemum stage involves a 'lowered symmetry detection threshold' where patterns 'lock into perfectly symmetrical structures.'
Corresponds to 'Level 4 — fully defined geometry': 'profoundly complex and fully structured' 2D patterns with an extensive color range.

also_noted: Augment: the onset mandala can be read as a Klüver spiral/lattice form constant driven to breakthrough intensity, its 'perfect symmetry' a product of a lowered symmetry-detection threshold (QRI) rather than an external object. Effect Index locates it near 'fully defined geometry' — profoundly complex, fully structured 2D pattern that saturates the field before opening into depth.

selected.name: The Carrier Wave
selected.description: An auditory-vibrational phenomenon at onset — a high-pitched ringing tone, droning frequency, or buzzing 'carrier wave' that resonates 'in every cell of the body,' often paired with a perceptual 'wobble' as the visual field destabilizes. McKenna heard 'a sound like the crumpling of a plastic bread wrapper... and a tone. A hummmm.'

sources.detail: 'After a launch, travelers often hear a ringing tone or vibration somewhat resembling a carrier wave... resonating in every cell of the body.'
'a sound like the crumpling of a plastic bread wrapper... and a tone. A hummmmmm.'
An auditory ringing-type sound reported in ~15.4% of reports.
'Acceleration, Acute' — 'a constantly rising, accelerating vibration felt through the entire body'; carrier tone 'sometimes steady, sometimes warbling up and down like a siren.'
High-volume auditory hallucinations of entities 'chattering, twittering' layered over the onset tone.

also_noted: Augment: the onset ring-tone is often experienced as an accelerating, rising vibration ('Acute Acceleration') felt through the whole body, and later couples to structured entity sound — the 'audio windup/windout' as beings arrive and depart. Strassman's volunteers add high-volume entity vocalizations layered over the tone.

selected.name: Living language / visible sound
selected.description: Synesthetic geometry in which heard sound becomes seen object — 'things heard become things seen.' McKenna's elves 'spoke in some kind of colored language which condensed into rotating machines'; survey participants saw hieroglyphs and ancient scripts.

sources.detail: Elves 'making objects come into existence by singing them into existence'; 'use your voice to make an object.'
Symbolic objects in ~17%: 'Egyptian hieroglyphical writings,' ancient language/hieroglyphics.
'Audioplasticity' — synesthetic entanglement of sounds and words with the visual field, the felt basis of 'seeing' language.
Structural typology includes visions of writing, scripts and symbols among figurative visual classes.

also_noted: Augment: the DMT-Nexus lexicon documents the mechanism — 'audioplasticity,' where 'sounds and words become entangled' across the senses — as the substrate of McKenna's visible Logos. Shanon's ayahuasca typology independently catalogs script/symbol visions, situating visible-language within a cross-tradition pattern.

selected.name: The Aperture / Iris Opening
selected.description: A recurring threshold image: the spinning onset mandala or a central point dilates open like a camera iris, a flower unfurling, a sphincter or a mechanical shutter, revealing depth and a space beyond. Where the Chrysanthemum can act as a closed door, the aperture is the moment it irises open and admits the traveler. Frequently reported as a bright central point or 'central light' that widens into a tunnel-mouth or portal, or as a magic-eye-like resolving of flat texture into an opening one is pulled through. Distinct from the tunnel-flight that often follows: the aperture is the dilation event itself, the opening of the way.
selected.science_note: Consistent with Klüver's 'tunnel/funnel' form constant and the retinocortical map, in which concentric/radial cortical activity is perceived as a central opening or funnel expanding outward from the visual-field center.

sources.detail: 'The Chrysanthemum... turns into a doorway, either welcoming or blocking access to breakthrough Hyperspace'; 'Central Light' described as an intelligent, sun-like source 'ontologically central to all existence.'
'Magic Eye' stage: flat texture resolves into depth so that 'the surfaces of the world-sheet' open into 3D forms and passageways.
22% of accounts (8/36) reported breaking through a 'veil or membrane' that parts to admit them into the breakthrough space.

selected.name: Zooming / Rushing Tunnel Flight
selected.description: The 'rush': an overwhelming sensation of acceleration and forward (or upward) motion — being pulled, sucked, launched or elevatored at unimaginable speed through a tunnel, vortex or stack of dimensional layers. Often paired with a rising vibratory tone and a feeling of the body's 'vibratory rate' climbing. Travelers report a 'dimensional elevator' that rises through successive vistas, each opening a chance to exit; or a tornado/typhoon of sensation that sweeps them under. The visual correlate is streaming radial motion — walls of pattern flying past — typically resolving at the far end into the waiting room or breakthrough space.
selected.science_note: The tunnel-with-forward-flow percept corresponds to Klüver's tunnel/funnel form constant animated by expanding concentric activity in V1; the retinocortical map renders outward-spreading cortical excitation as motion toward or through a central aperture.

sources.detail: 'Acceleration, Acute' — 'a constantly rising, accelerating vibration felt through the entire body'; 'Dimensional Elevator' — a small rising space 'ascending through a multitude of higher & extra dimensional spaces,' opening periodically on new vistas.
39% (14/36) described intense sensory onset events — 'it came like a typhoon over me' and being 'in the middle of a tornado, everything was going at unimaginable speed.'
Volunteers reported 'a startlingly rapid onset' and a sense of consciousness being separated from and rushed away from the body.

selected.name: Breathing & Liquid Surfaces
selected.description: At and around threshold, ordinary surfaces begin to breathe, ripple, melt and flow — walls pulsing in and out, floors rolling in slow waves, edges softening as if everything were made of liquid, wax or living tissue. Objects seem to inhale and exhale in time with the traveler; textures crawl and reflow; solid matter takes on a wet, gel-like or candy-like plasticity. This animate-liquid quality is often the first sign the substance has taken hold (in the ambient, eyes-open phase) and returns during the descent as hyperspace 'melts' back into the room.
selected.science_note: Corresponds to Effect Index/PsychonautWiki 'drifting' (morphing/breathing/flowing/melting) effects and to low-level geometry animating static surfaces — attributed to unstable, continuously updated edge and motion processing under the drug.

sources.detail: Lower-intensity visual effects include continuous morphing, breathing and flowing of surfaces before defined geometry takes over.
'Plasmatis' — 'the multicolored constantly shifting gel-goo' decorating space; 'Candyland' — reality 'as if made of colorful candy,' polished and plastic.
Reports of surfaces and forms in continuous fluid transformation as a baseline feature of the visual style.

sources.author: Terence McKenna
sources.work: True Hallucinations / The Archaic Revival / lectures
sources.note: Coined 'self-transforming machine elves,' 'tykes,' 'jeweled self-dribbling basketballs,' 'syntax-driving light,' and the visible-language / Logos themes. A vivid individual account, not a representative sample.

sources.author: Rick Strassman, M.D.
sources.note: Univ. of New Mexico clinical study, ~60 volunteers / ~400 doses (1990–1995). Source of 'they were waiting for me,' the high-tech nursery/lab realms, and the abduction-overlap observation. Clinical narrative, not a controlled frequency study.

sources.author: Davis, Clifton, Weaver, Hurwitz, Johnson & Griffiths (Johns Hopkins)
sources.work: Survey of entity encounter experiences occasioned by inhaled N,N-DMT
sources.note: Journal of Psychopharmacology. N=2,561 — the largest DMT entity survey. Descriptor %, benevolence, fear, reality-alteration and belief-change figures. Some figures here drawn from the abstract + reputable secondary summaries where the full text was paywalled; treat exact decimals as approximate.

sources.author: Lawrence, Carhart-Harris, Griffiths & Timmermann
sources.work: Phenomenology and content of the inhaled N,N-DMT experience
sources.note: Scientific Reports. Content analysis of 3,778 r/DMT reports — the source of the entity-phenotype and realm/geometry percentages. Samples people who self-select to post, so rates reflect that population.

sources.author: Michael, Luke & Robinson
sources.work: An Encounter With the Other: a thematic & content analysis of DMT experiences from a naturalistic field study
sources.note: Frontiers in Psychology. n=36 breakthrough-dose field study — beings 94%, other-space 100%, the role/appearance/demeanor breakdowns, the realm taxonomy (lattice/circus/machine worlds).

sources.author: Timmermann, Roseman, Williams, Carhart-Harris et al. (Imperial College)
sources.note: Frontiers in Psychology. Placebo-controlled comparison: DMT reproduces much of the Greyson NDE-scale profile; authors caution the contexts differ.

sources.author: Timmermann, Roseman, Schartner, Carhart-Harris et al. (Imperial College)
sources.work: Neural correlates of the DMT experience assessed with multivariate EEG
sources.note: Scientific Reports. N=13. Peak subjective effect 2–3 min after IV dose, elevated ~17 min; alpha-power drop and rising signal diversity.

sources.author: David Luke
sources.work: Discarnate entities and dimethyltryptamine (DMT): psychopharmacology, phenomenology and ontology
sources.note: J. Society for Psychical Research. Foundational typology of recurrent entity types (elves, mantis 'surgeons,' jewel-encrusted reptilians) across independent reporters.

sources.author: Benny Shanon
sources.work: The Antipodes of the Mind: charting the phenomenology of the ayahuasca experience
sources.note: Oxford University Press. The most thorough systematic phenomenology of the closely related (same-molecule) ayahuasca state — serpents, royalty/palaces, temples, death/rebirth.

sources.author: Peter Meyer
sources.work: 340 DMT Trip Reports (and 'Concerning the Nature of the DMT Entities')
sources.note: Canonical early archive: 226 of 340 reports (~66%) mention apparently independent entities; argues their cross-report consistency makes them 'intersubjectively verifiable.'

sources.author: Jennifer A. Lyke (Stockton University)
sources.work: DMT Entities: not everyone gets machine elves (analysis of 149 Erowid reports)
sources.note: Quantifies how the folk vocabulary maps to actual report frequencies — the corrective that 'machine elves' (~2.9%) is rarer than 'feminine' (~24%) or even 'robot/machine entity' (~6.7%).

sources.author: DMT-Nexus community
sources.note: Crowd-authored glossary that names the territory (Hyperspace, Breakthrough, Waiting Room, Chrysanthemum, Carrier Wave, the Void, Hyperslap, Machine Elves/Tykes). Folk-phenomenology; some entries are one contributor's idiosyncratic coinages.

sources.author: Erowid
sources.note: Large archive of first-person reports underlying many of the secondary analyses.

sources.author: Andrés Gómez Emilsson (Qualia Research Institute)
sources.work: The Hyperbolic Geometry of DMT Experiences
sources.note: A six-level model (Threshold, Chrysanthemum, Magic Eye, Waiting Room, Breakthrough, Amnesia) and the argument that the geometry is hyperbolic, which explains its un-rememberability. An interpretive theory, not established fact.

sources.author: David Jay Brown & Sara Phinn Huntley
sources.work: The Illustrated Field Guide to DMT Entities
sources.note: A 25-entity taxonomy synthesizing the popular literature; provides structured entity categories (qualitative, not frequency-measured).

sources.author: John E. Mack, M.D.
sources.note: Harvard psychiatrist who documented the abduction 'examination' script. Heavily criticized for hypnosis/suggestion methodology; presented alongside the skeptical counter-explanation.

sources.author: Graham St John
sources.work: The Breakthrough Experience: DMT hyperspace and its liminal aesthetics
sources.note: Anthropology of Consciousness. Liminality framing; hyperspace as infinite cathedrals/machine-scapes/geometric abstraction; the 'Universal/Gaian Mind' perceived as God.

sources.author: Josie Kins (and contributors)
sources.work: Effect Index / Subjective Effect Index (incl. Autonomous Entity, geometry & DMT effect taxonomy)
sources.note: A community-built granular taxonomy of 200+ subjective psychedelic effects with definitions, subcomponents, and visual replications, including formal 'autonomous entity' and geometry classifications applied to DMT. Reliability class: structured community archive/taxonomy (systematic but not peer-reviewed).

sources.author: Heinrich Klüver
sources.note: Origin of the 'form constants': lattice/honeycomb, cobweb, tunnel/funnel, and spiral, observed across systematic mescaline self-experiments in bright, highly saturated colors. The foundational scientific taxonomy of visionary geometry; describes recurring forms, not a representative statistical sample.
